# agent_tools


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A host agent, such as Leela, makes a walk, reads its state, grades an
answer, notes a confusion, changes a walk, adds a source, restores an
old version, gives the data to explain the step on screen and knows
which page the learner sees. This module holds those operations. It
imports from `learner`, `models`, `sources`,
[`tutor`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#tutor),
`path` and
[`show`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#show). Each
operation takes the learner’s store `lr`, and the host’s model call
`ask(prompt, sp='')` when it needs a model. Only
[`create_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#create_walk),
[`record_attempt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#record_attempt)
and
[`change_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#change_walk)
call a model.
[`explain_here`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#explain_here)
calls none: the agent writes the explanation from its data.

**The contract of every operation**

- An operation returns one dict with these fields: `status` (`'ok'`,
  `'error'` or `'stopped'`), `operation_id`, `vault`, `walk`, `step`,
  `revision`, `data` (a dict) and `error`.
  [`result`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#result)
  builds it.
- `error` is `None`, or one of `ERRORS`: `'vault_locked'`,
  `'read_only'`, `'source_missing'`, `'model_refused'`,
  `'privacy_refused'`, `'stopped'`, `'not_found'`, `'attempt_conflict'`,
  `'stale_state'`. A host adds its own names for one call with `extra`:
  `failed('thread_busy', extra=('thread_busy',))`.
- The host owns privacy.
  [`create_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#create_walk)
  takes `guard(text) -> text` from the host and runs no engine guard of
  its own.
  [`record_attempt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#record_attempt)
  takes the `revision` that the caller last saw and refuses an old one
  with `'stale_state'`.
- An expected failure never raises. It has `status` `'error'` and an
  `error`, and `data['message']` says why. A stop has `status`
  `'stopped'` and `error` `'stopped'`.
- The values are JSON values only. The caller owns `operation_id`: the
  engine leaves it `None`. `vault` is the file name of the vault.
  `revision` is the `updated` time of the walk.
- Stop is a `stopping()` callback that returns true after a stop. The
  operation checks it before each model call and after each one, so
  before it saves anything. A stop leaves no partial walk.
- `TOOLS` lists each operation that a host makes a tool, with the
  arguments that the model gives. The host gives `lr`, `ask`, `stopping`
  and `progress` itself, and for
  [`explain_here`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#explain_here)
  also `jid` and `i`: the step on the page that the learner sees.
  `READS` names the tools that change nothing.
- A change to a walk takes the `revision` that the caller last saw, and
  refuses an old one with `'stale_state'`. Each change is one change
  with an Undo in the history of the walk, so
  [`list_versions`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#list_versions)
  and
  [`restore_version`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#restore_version)
  see it.

Import what this module uses. The model, the walk and the tutor come
from the engine modules above it.

## The result

[`result`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#result)
builds the one shape.
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#failed)
builds an expected failure: a stop has the status `'stopped'`, and each
other failure has the status `'error'`.

### result

``` python
def result(
    status:str, # one of `STATUSES`
    extra:tuple=(), # error names that the host adds to `ERRORS`, for this call only
    **kw
)->dict: # a value for any field of `FIELDS`
```

*The one result shape: `status` and each field of `FIELDS`, empty unless
`kw` gives it.*

`TOOLS` names each operation that a host makes a tool. The arguments are
the ones that the model gives. They have the names of the function
parameters, so a host passes them straight through.

A failure has the status `'error'`, its `error` and a message. A stop
has its own status. A name that is not in `ERRORS` is refused.

This cell checks both.

``` python
test_eq((failed('not_found', 'no walk')['status'], failed('stopped')['status'], result('ok')['error']), ('error', 'stopped', None))
test_fail(lambda: failed('broken'), contains='no error')
test_fail(lambda: failed('thread_busy'), contains='no error')
test_eq((failed('thread_busy', extra=('thread_busy',))['error'], result('error', error='mode_off', extra=('mode_off',))['error']), ('thread_busy', 'mode_off'))
test_eq(set(ERRORS) & {'conflict', 'withheld', 'no_source'}, set())
```

## Errors that the contract names

[`_run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#_run)
turns the errors that the contract names into results. Any other error
is a bug, so it stays an error.

A stop is a `BaseException`. The tutor has `except Exception` blocks,
and they must not swallow it. A host model call that declines raises
[`ModelRefused`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#modelrefused).
A reply that is not JSON after two tries is a `ValueError` from
[`ask_json`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/models.html#ask_json),
and it also counts as a refusal.

The vault has no read-only or locked flag. A failed write shows as an
SQLite error, so
[`vault_failure`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#vault_failure)
reads the class names and the message.

### ModelRefused

``` python

    *args, **kwargs

```

*What a host `ask` raises when the model declines to answer.*

A real SQLite error and a real apsw error give the two vault failures.
Other errors give none. The word `blocked` is not `locked`.

``` python
import apsw, sqlite3
```

``` python
test_eq([vault_failure(e) for e in (apsw.ReadOnlyError('x'), apsw.BusyError('x'), sqlite3.OperationalError('attempt to write a readonly database'),
                                     sqlite3.OperationalError('database is locked'), KeyError('blocked'))],
        ['read_only', 'vault_locked', 'read_only', 'vault_locked', None])
```

## Make a walk

[`create_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#create_walk)
calls
[`walk_from_topic`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#walk_from_topic)
with the host’s `ask`. It reports three stages to `progress`, with the
part done from 0 to 1:

- `'planning'` goes out before the model call.
- `'sources'` goes out at each search for the passage of a step.
- `'steps'` goes out when the steps are saved.

`stopping()` is checked before and after each model call, and before
each search. The planner saves the walk before it looks for passages, so
a stop in that stage drops the new walk. A stop leaves no partial walk.

The goal first passes
[`guard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/models.html#guard). A
goal with personal data goes to the model redacted, and
`data['redacted']` is true. The walk keeps the goal that the learner
wrote as its title. A goal that the guard refuses gives `withheld`, and
no model call is made.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L134"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### create_walk

``` python
def create_walk(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, # the learner's store
    ask, # the host model call, `ask(prompt, sp='')`
    goal:str, # what the learner wants to learn
    stopping:function=<lambda>, # true after a stop
    progress:function=<lambda>, # told the stage ('planning', 'sources', 'steps') and the part done
    settings:dict | None=None, # the host's values of the settings rows (row name to value), for this call only; None reads the settings file
    guard:NoneType=None, # the host's privacy check, `guard(text) -> text`; it may raise `Withheld`; None sends the goal as it is
    research:NoneType=None, # whether to look for web sources after the walk is saved: True, False, 'yes' or 'no'; None means yes when `gather` is given
    gather:NoneType=None, # the host's `gather(jid)`, which returns an object with `why`; the only way that `create_walk` looks at the web
)->dict:
```

*Plan a walk to `goal` with the host model and save it, with a passage
from the vault
([`VaultSource`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#vaultsource))
for each step; web sources come from the host
[`gather`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#gather) hook,
after the walk is saved, when `research` allows it.*

### plain

``` python
def plain(
    text
)->str:
```

*`text` on one line, as the person said it: no host note block
(`<beat>…</beat>`), context block or `<user-request>` wrapper.*

The host owns privacy. `guard(text)` returns the text to send, or raises
[`Withheld`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/models.html#withheld).
With `guard=None` the goal goes out unchanged. A redacted goal sets
`redacted` in the result, and the saved title is still the learner’s own
goal.

``` python
import json
from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import guard as _guard
```

``` python
_plan = json.dumps(dict(title='Ranking', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name='Ranking', statement='Ranking orders items by a score.', ways=['words'])]))
_mail, _asked = 'learn ranking for jane.doe@example.com', []
_ask = lambda p, sp='': _asked.append(p) or _plan
_r = create_walk(temp_learning(), _ask, _mail, guard=lambda s: _guard(s, mode='refuse'))
test_eq((_r['error'], _asked), ('privacy_refused', []))
_lr = temp_learning()
_r = create_walk(_lr, _ask, _mail, guard=lambda s: _guard(s, mode='redact'))
test_eq((_r['data']['redacted'], 'jane.doe@example.com' in ' '.join(_asked), _lr.journey(_r['walk']).title), (True, False, _mail))
_asked.clear()
_r = create_walk(temp_learning(), _ask, _mail)
test_eq((_r['data']['redacted'], 'jane.doe@example.com' in ' '.join(_asked)), (False, True))
```

[`create_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#create_walk)
looks at the web only through the host `gather(jid)` hook, after the
walk is saved. `research` is true by default when the host gives
[`gather`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#gather), and
`'no'` skips it. A walk that the learner stops during research keeps the
passages that were found, and `data['research']` says in words how many
ideas got a source. The hook is the only call to a model or to the web
that this adds.

``` python
_said = []
_g = lambda jid: _said.append(jid) or AttrDict(why='Searched the web and read 1 page: 1 of 1 idea got a source, and 0 did not.')
_r = create_walk(temp_learning(), _ask, 'learn ranking', gather=_g)
test_eq((_r['data']['research'][:12], _said == [_r['walk']]), ('Searched the', True))
for _off in ('no', False):
    _said.clear(); _r = create_walk(temp_learning(), _ask, 'learn ranking', gather=_g, research=_off)
    test_eq(('research' in _r['data'], _said), (False, []))
_r = create_walk(temp_learning(), _ask, 'learn ranking')
test_eq('research' in _r['data'], False)
def _boom(jid): raise RuntimeError('no web')
test_eq(create_walk(temp_learning(), _ask, 'learn ranking', gather=_boom)['data']['research'], 'Research stopped: no web.')
```

A host can put a note block of its own, `<beat>…</beat>`, in a message.
[`plain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#plain)
takes it out of the goal and out of the words of a change, so no note of
the host becomes the text of a walk.

``` python
test_eq(plain('learn ranking\n\n<beat>\nabhyasa-index: no callback registered\n</beat>'), 'learn ranking')
test_eq(plain('learn <BEAT> never closed'), 'learn')
test_eq(plain('<notebook path="a">x</notebook>\n\n<user-request>\nI don\'t get this\n</user-request>'), "I don't get this")
test_eq(plain('<user-request> I don\'t get this'), "I don't get this")
_asked.clear(); _r = create_walk(temp_learning(), _ask, 'learn ranking <beat> x: failed </beat>')
test_eq((any('beat' in p for p in _asked), _r['status']), (False, 'ok'))
```

## Read a walk

[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#walk_state)
gives the steps of a walk as plain data. A step has a `quote` only when
its stored passage has text and a link. The text is the stored source
text, not a model summary. A step without one has `quote: None` and
`ungrounded: True`.

The `gauge` is the engine’s own
[`understanding`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#understanding):
depth, state and recall. This module adds no score. A step that is done,
skipped or known has no `check`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L191"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    settings:dict | None=None, # the host's values of the settings rows, for this call only; None reads the settings file
)->dict:
```

*The walk as plain data: its steps with their quote or `ungrounded` and
their checks, and the gauge of each concept.*

## Answer a check

[`record_attempt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#record_attempt)
uses the grading path of the web walk: `path.open_short` opens the check
with
[`Tutor.ask_on`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#tutor.ask_on),
and
[`Tutor.answer`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#tutor.answer)
grades it and saves the attempt with
[`Learning.record`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#learning.record).
This module has no grader of its own.

The `attempt_id` goes in the meta of the question, so
[`Learning.record`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#learning.record)
keeps it on the attempt. A key is read on (walk, step). The same key
with the same answer gives the stored result, with no new model call.
The same key with another answer is a `conflict`. A step that is already
answered is also a `conflict`.

The result has the gauge of the concept after the answer.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L223"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### record_attempt

``` python
def record_attempt(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, # the learner's store
    jid:str, # the walk id
    i:int, # the place of the step in the walk
    answer:str, # the learner's answer
    attempt_id:str, # the key of this answer, made once by the caller
    ask, # the host model call, `ask(prompt, sp='')`
    settings:dict | None=None, # the host's values of the settings rows, for this call only; None reads the settings file
    revision:NoneType=None, # the `revision` of the walk that the caller last saw; another value gives `stale_state`; None skips the check
)->dict:
```

*Grade the answer to the short check of step `i` and save the attempt,
once for each `attempt_id`; it cannot be stopped and reports no
progress, because the grade is short.*

A call that carries an old `revision` of the walk is refused with
`'stale_state'`, and `data['revision']` holds the current one. It sends
nothing to the model and saves nothing.

``` python
from abhyasa.learner import NO_CHECK, temp_learning
```

``` python
_lr = temp_learning()
_lr.put_journey(dict(id='w1', title='T', goal='g', subject='ml', mode='walk', created=time.time(), steps=[dict(slug='ranking', status='todo', read=None, check=dict(NO_CHECK))]))
_rev = _lr.journey('w1').get('updated')
_stale = record_attempt(_lr, 'w1', 0, 'x', 'k1', None, revision='old')
test_eq((_stale['error'], _stale['data']['revision'], _stale['revision']), ('stale_state', _rev, _rev))
test_eq(_lr.attempts('ranking', limit=None), [])
```

## Note a confusion

[`note_confusion`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#note_confusion)
keeps what confuses the learner in the profile, in the line `Name: note`
that [`show`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#show)
writes for “Not clear” feedback. The tutor reads that line when it
writes the next question and lesson. A confusion is not an answer: it
makes no attempt and does not change the concept. The text goes through
[`clean_note`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#clean_note)
first. A note with no text records nothing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L256"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    note:str, # what confuses the learner, in their words
)->dict:
```

*Keep what confuses the learner on step `i`; it is no answer and changes
no concept.*

## Run the code of a step

[`record_code_attempt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#record_code_attempt)
files the run of the code of step `i` as an attempt, with no model: the
host graded it
([`grade_code`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#grade_code))
and gives `ok`. A right run counts at depth 3 for the method `code`, a
wrong one at depth 2, as a demo prediction does. The result is the one
of
[`record_attempt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#record_attempt),
with the gauge. The same `attempt_id` gives the saved attempt again and
changes nothing more. A step with a check that is still open is not
closed by it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L273"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def record_code_attempt(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, # the learner's store
    jid:str, # the walk id
    i:int, # the place of the step in the walk
    ok:bool, # whether the run met the `expect` of the step
    attempt_id:str, # the key of this run, made once by the caller
    note:str='', # what the learner ran, one line
)->dict:
```

*File one graded run of the code of step `i` as an attempt, once for
each `attempt_id`, with no model.*

``` python
from abhyasa.learner import NO_CHECK, temp_learning
```

``` python
_lc = temp_learning(); _lc.put('Ranking', 'A rank is the place of an item in a list.', 'ml', core='A rank orders items.')
_lc.put_journey(dict(id='wk', title='T', goal='g', subject='ml', mode='walk', created=time.time(), steps=[dict(slug='ranking', status='todo', read=None, check=dict(NO_CHECK), code=dict(src='x = 3', watch=['x'], expect=dict(var='x', value='4')))]))
_a = record_code_attempt(_lc, 'wk', 0, True, 'c1', 'x = 4')
test_eq((_a['status'], _a['data']['correct'], _a['data']['done']), ('ok', True, False))
_n = len(_lc.attempts('ranking', limit=None)); _g = _a['data']['gauge']
_b = record_code_attempt(_lc, 'wk', 0, True, 'c1', 'x = 4')
test_eq((len(_lc.attempts('ranking', limit=None)), _b['data']['gauge']), (_n, _g))   # the same id: nothing more
test_eq(record_code_attempt(_lc, 'wk', 0, False, 'c2')['data']['correct'], False)
test_eq(record_code_attempt(_lc, 'nope', 0, True, 'c3')['error'], 'not_found')
```

## Change a walk

The editor of the web walk is in `path`:
[`edit_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#edit_walk)
applies one change to the steps and keeps it, with the old steps, in the
history of the walk. Each tool here is one such change, so one Undo
takes it back.

Each tool takes the `revision` that the caller last saw.
[`_open`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#_open)
gives the walk, or the failure: `not_found` for a walk that is not
there, `stale_state` for a revision that is old. A change by hand never
calls the model:
[`keep_idea`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#keep_idea)
locks an idea, so that the builder and the box leave it as it is,
[`drop_idea`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#drop_idea)
removes it and
[`move_idea`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#move_idea)
gives it a new place from 1. The idea is its slug, or its number from 1.
A change by hand unlocks the idea that it changes, as in the web editor.

### keep_idea

``` python
def keep_idea(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, jid:str, idea:str, revision:NoneType=None
)->dict:
```

*Keep the idea: the builder and the box of the walk do not change it. It
is one change, with an Undo.*

A walk of three ideas shows the three tools. Moving an idea to a place
that is not in the walk is refused, and the walk stays as it was. An old
`revision` gives `stale_state`, and an idea that is not there gives
`not_found`.

``` python
_PLAN = json.dumps(dict(title='Ranking', subject='ml', steps=[dict(name=n, statement=f'{n} is one idea of ranking.', ways=['words']) for n in ('Scores', 'Ranks', 'Fusion')]))
def _fresh():
    lr = temp_learning()
    return lr, create_walk(lr, lambda p, sp='': _PLAN, 'learn ranking')['walk']
_lr, _jid = _fresh()
_k, _m = keep_idea(_lr, _jid, '1'), move_idea(_lr, _jid, 'scores', 3)
test_eq((_k['status'], _k['data']['changed'], _lr.journey(_jid).steps[2]['slug'], _m['data']['ideas']), ('ok', True, 'scores', ['ranks', 'fusion', 'scores']))
test_eq((move_idea(_lr, _jid, 'ranks', 9)['error'], [s['slug'] for s in _lr.journey(_jid).steps]), ('model_refused', ['ranks', 'fusion', 'scores']))
test_eq((drop_idea(_lr, _jid, 'nope')['error'], drop_idea(_lr, 'nope', '1')['error'], keep_idea(_lr, _jid, '1', revision='old')['error']), ('not_found', 'not_found', 'stale_state'))
_d = drop_idea(_lr, _jid, 'fusion', revision=_m['revision'])
test_eq((_d['status'], _d['data']['ideas']), ('ok', ['ranks', 'scores']))
```

## Change a walk from words

[`change_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#change_walk)
is the box at the top of the web walk, for the agent. It asks the host
model for the changes (`path.propose`), and makes them as one change
with an Undo (`path.improve_walk`). A locked idea never changes. A
change of the kind "look for a source" is not made here: the idea is in
`data['sources_wanted']`, and the host calls
[`add_source`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#add_source).

`stopping()` is checked before and after each model call, and
[`improve_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#improve_walk)
saves only after its last model call. A stop leaves the walk as it was.
A walk that changed during the model calls gives `stale_state`, and
nothing is saved. The model sees the words of the learner only through
`ask`, so the host guard sees them:
[`Withheld`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/models.html#withheld)
gives `privacy_refused`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L352"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### change_walk

``` python
def change_walk(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, # the learner's store
    ask, # the host model call, `ask(prompt, sp='')`
    jid:str, # the walk id
    instruction:str, # what the learner wants to change, in their words
    stopping:function=<lambda>, # true after a stop
    settings:dict | None=None, # the host's values of the settings rows, for this call only
    revision:NoneType=None, # the `revision` of the walk that the caller last saw; another value gives `stale_state`
)->dict:
```

*Change walk `jid` from the words of the learner, as one change with an
Undo.*

A scripted model that asks for one change gives one change with an Undo.
A stop before the call, a refusal of the guard and an old revision each
leave the walk as it was.

``` python
_lr, _jid = _fresh()
_say = lambda *ch: (lambda p, sp='': json.dumps(dict(changes=list(ch))))
_r = change_walk(_lr, _say(dict(op='skip', idea='ranks', why='you asked')), _jid, 'skip the ranks idea')
test_eq((_r['status'], _r['data']['changed'], _r['data']['changes'][0]['op'], _lr.journey(_jid).steps[1]['status'], len(_lr.edits('walk', _jid))), ('ok', True, 'skip', 'skip', 1))
_before = _lr.journey(_jid)
test_eq((change_walk(_lr, _say(), _jid, 'x', stopping=lambda: True)['status'], change_walk(_lr, (lambda p, sp='': (_ for _ in ()).throw(Withheld('no'))), _jid, 'x')['error'],
         change_walk(_lr, _say(), _jid, 'x', revision='old')['error'], change_walk(_lr, _say(), 'nope', 'x')['error']), ('stopped', 'privacy_refused', 'stale_state', 'not_found'))
test_eq(_lr.journey(_jid), _before)
```

## Add a source

[`add_source`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#add_source)
files a source with the engine’s own filers (`path.file_chip`), as the
walk block does, with no second agent. A link, a path to a file or a
folder, or a chip id goes in. The chip joins the chips of the walk, with
its count and its filing record, and the ideas that have no passage get
one word for word from the new documents. All of that is one change with
an Undo. A source that gives no document is `source_missing`, and the
walk stays as it was.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L387"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### add_source

``` python
def add_source(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, # the learner's store
    jid:str, # the walk id
    source:str, # a link, a path to a file or a folder, or a chip id
    settings:dict | None=None, # the host's values of the settings rows, for this call only
    revision:NoneType=None, # the `revision` of the walk that the caller last saw; another value gives `stale_state`
)->dict:
```

*File `source` and add it to walk `jid`, with a passage for each idea
that has none; one change with an Undo.*

A document in the vault is a source, as a `doc:` chip. Its passage goes
to each idea that has none, word for word, and the change has an Undo. A
path that is not there gives `source_missing`. (A file or a folder goes
through the same filer, which reads only files in the home folder.)

``` python
_lr, _jid = _fresh()
_d = _lr.vault.add([(0, 'Ranking\n\nRanks and scores are two ideas of ranking. A score is a number for one item, and a rank is the place of an item in a list. ' * 2)], 'Ranking notes', source='https://example.org/notes', kind='web')['doc_id']
_r = add_source(_lr, _jid, f'doc:{_d}')
test_eq((_r['status'], _r['data']['changed'], _r['data']['documents'], len(_lr.journey(_jid)['chips']), len(_lr.edits('walk', _jid))), ('ok', True, 1, 1, 1))
test_eq((add_source(_lr, _jid, f'doc:{_d}')['data']['changed'], add_source(_lr, _jid, '/nowhere/x.md')['error'], add_source(_lr, 'nope', f'doc:{_d}')['error'], add_source(_lr, _jid, 'x', revision='old')['error']), (False, 'source_missing', 'not_found', 'stale_state'))
```

## Earlier versions

[`list_versions`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#list_versions)
gives the history of the walk, newest first: the number of each version,
the words that say what changed, who changed it, and whether it can come
back.
[`restore_version`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#restore_version)
goes back to the version before one change, as a new change, with
`path.restore_walk`. Number 1 is the newest.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L428"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### restore_version

``` python
def restore_version(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, jid:str, version:int, revision:NoneType=None
)->dict:
```

*Go back to the version of walk `jid` before the change `version` of
[`list_versions`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#list_versions),
as a new change with an Undo.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L419"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### list_versions

``` python
def list_versions(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, jid:str
)->dict:
```

*The earlier versions of walk `jid`, newest first; number 1 is the
newest.*

Two changes make two versions. Restoring the older one brings back the
walk as it was before the first change, and that is a third change.

``` python
_lr, _jid = _fresh()
keep_idea(_lr, _jid, '1'); drop_idea(_lr, _jid, '3')
_v = list_versions(_lr, _jid)['data']['versions']
test_eq(([v['version'] for v in _v], [v['restorable'] for v in _v]), ([1, 2], [True, True]))
_r = restore_version(_lr, _jid, 2)
test_eq((_r['status'], _r['data']['ideas'], len(list_versions(_lr, _jid)['data']['versions'])), ('ok', ['scores', 'ranks', 'fusion'], 3))
test_eq((restore_version(_lr, _jid, 9)['error'], restore_version(_lr, _jid, 1, revision='old')['error'], list_versions(_lr, 'nope')['error']), ('not_found', 'stale_state', 'not_found'))
```

## Explain the step on screen

[`explain_here`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#explain_here)
is for "I don’t get this". The host knows which step the learner sees
(`jid` and `i`), and the model gives only the `note`: what the learner
does not get. The operation makes **no model call**: a tool that calls a
model inside a turn of the same session can wait for the lock that the
turn holds. It gives the agent the data to teach with, and the agent
writes the explanation in its own next message: the idea and its
statement, the passage word for word (or `ungrounded`), the gauge, the
level line, the words of the learner, and `rules`. When the gauge says
the idea is new, a gap or shaky, or a need is missing or shaky,
`simpler` is true and the rules ask for short numbered steps. The rules
say nothing of an answer that the learner did not give.

The tool keeps the note with
[`note_confusion`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#note_confusion),
as the tool of that name does, and only when the data is ready. A note
with no words, a walk or step that is not there, or an old `revision`
keeps nothing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L444"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### explain_here

``` python
def explain_here(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, # the learner's store
    jid:str, # the walk the learner sees
    i:int, # the step the learner sees
    note:str, # what the learner does not get, in their words
    settings:dict | None=None, # the host's values of the settings rows, for this call only
    revision:NoneType=None, # the `revision` of the walk that the caller last saw; another value gives `stale_state`
)->dict:
```

*The data to teach step `i` of walk `jid` to a learner who does not get
it, and the rules for the explanation; the agent writes it. It keeps
what confuses the learner. It calls no model.*

The data holds the passage and the words of the learner, and the
confusion is kept. A new idea is `simpler`. The failures keep nothing,
and no model is called, so the tool has no `ask`.

``` python
_lr, _jid = _fresh()
_r = explain_here(_lr, _jid, 0, 'what is a score')
test_eq((_r['status'], _r['data']['simpler'], _r['data']['ungrounded'], _r['data']['recorded'], _r['data']['confusion'], 'numbered steps' in _r['data']['rules']), ('ok', True, True, True, 'what is a score', True))
_lr2, _jid2 = _fresh()
test_eq((explain_here(_lr2, _jid2, 9, 'q')['error'], explain_here(_lr2, _jid2, 0, 'q', revision='old')['error'], explain_here(_lr2, 'nope', 0, 'q')['error'], explain_here(_lr2, _jid2, 0, ' ')['error'], list(_lr2.profile().confuses)),
        ('not_found', 'stale_state', 'not_found', 'model_refused', []))
```

## Context for the agent

[`learner_context`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#learner_context)
is a short block of plain text for a system prompt: the open walk and
step, its gauge, and the rule for sources. The rule comes first, so a
cut at `n` characters never removes it. With no `i`, the step is the
current one.

With `page`, the path that the learner sees in the Learn tab, the block
says what is on screen.
[`page_of`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#page_of)
reads the path: `/w/<walk>/<i>` is a step, `/w/<walk>` a walk,
`/c/<slug>` a concept, and `/you`, `/graph`, `/library`, `/t/<talk>`,
`/talk/...` and `/` are the other pages. A walk page gives the walk, and
a step page gives the step too. Both win over the walk and the step that
the host passes, because the page is what the learner looks at. The line
on screen comes right after the rule, so a cut keeps it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L488"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### learner_context

``` python
def learner_context(
    lr:abhyasa.learner.Learning, # the learner's store
    jid:str=None, # the open walk, if any
    i:int=None, # the open step; the current step when None
    n:int=1200, # the most characters
    page:str=None, # the path that the Learn tab shows; the walk and step of the page win over `jid` and `i`
)->str:
```

*A short plain-text block for a system prompt: what is on screen, the
open walk and step, its gauge, and the rule for sources.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/agent_tools.py#L473"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### page_of

``` python
def page_of(
    page:str
)->dict:
```

*The Abhyasa page at the path `page` as `dict(kind, jid, i, slug)`;
`kind` is step, walk, concept, you, graph, library, talk, today or
other, and ’’ for no path.*

The page path gives a step, a walk or a concept. A step page wins over
the step that the host passes, and a query or the old `/learn/abh`
prefix does not matter. The context names the step on screen with its
quote or `ungrounded`, and it stays in the cap.

``` python
test_eq([page_of(p)['kind'] for p in ('/w/a/2?pane=1', '/w/a', '/w/a/start', '/c/x', '/you/strengths', '/graph', '/library/graph', '/library', '/t/9', '/talk/new', '/', '', '/zzz')],
        ['step', 'walk', 'walk', 'concept', 'you', 'graph', 'graph', 'library', 'talk', 'talk', 'today', '', 'other'])
test_eq((page_of('/learn/abh/w/a%20b/2')['jid'], page_of('/w/a/2')['i'], page_of('/c/x')['slug']), ('a b', 2, 'x'))
_lr, _jid = _fresh()
_c = learner_context(_lr, None, page=f'/w/{_jid}/1?x=1')
test_eq(('Step 2 of 3: Ranks' in _c, 'explain_here' in _c, 'ungrounded' in _c, RULE in _c, len(learner_context(_lr, page=f'/w/{_jid}/1', n=300)) <= 301), (True, True, True, True, True))
test_eq(('Step 3 of 3' in learner_context(_lr, _jid, 0, page=f'/w/{_jid}/2'), 'the graph page' in learner_context(_lr, page='/graph'), learner_context(_lr, page='/w/zz/0').endswith(RULE)), (True, True, True))
```
